title: Introduction to the *GraphExperiment* class
text: Networks (graphs) become widely used data representations biology, can efficiently encode node-node interactions neighborhoods. high-throughput, quantitative omics data (e.g., transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, epigenomics, etc), widely used network representations include gene coexpression, protein-protein interaction, gene regulatory, co-abundance networks. data structures store quantitative data associated metadata exist (e.g., SummarizedExperiment, SingleCellExperiment, SpatialExperiment, etc), support networks describing features relate currently missing. GraphExperiment S4 class extends SingleCellExperiment (Amezquita et al. 2020) include additional container networks associated assay features (graphs representing columns, samples cells, supported package). note, trees alternative way representing assay features related . Users interested tree representations assays rows/columns can use TreeSummarizedExperiment package. Trees essentially kind graph (.e., trees graphs, graphs trees). , chose use general graph representation (namely igraph objects) provide users developers flexibility.

title: Introduction to the *GraphExperiment* class
text: Since GraphExperiment class extends SingleCellExperiment class, SingleCellExperiment slots present GraphExperiment, including: assays: list matrices primary (e.g., counts) transformed (e.g., log-normalized counts, TPM, etc) data, features rows observations columns. colData: data frame column (observation) metadata, sample ID, condition, batch ID, genotype, etc. rowData: data frame row (feature) metadata, gene ID, genomic coordinates, functional annotation, etc. reducedDims: list data frames reduced dimensions, PCA, t-SNE, UMAP embeddings. Compared SingleCellExperiment objects, GraphExperiment provides additional container: graphs: list igraph objects containing graphs, including (optional) node edge attributes. Graphs used represent features (rows, columns) relate .1 GraphExperiment class. igraph data class igraph package standard data structure graph representation R. unfamiliar igraph objects, can learn reading igraph vignettes.

Compared SingleCellExperiment objects, difference last row, indicates object contains graph named ‘cor’. Importantly, since nodes graphs always sync rownames, feature IDs rownames graph node names need . example, attempting create GraphExperiment object features rownames missing lead error: Alternatively, can create GraphExperiment object coercing existing (Ranged)SummarizedExperiment SingleCellExperiment object. example: Note graphs container still , empty. access names graphs, use graphNames() function.

list(gene_ids, cell_ids)) mat[1:5, 1:5] #>       cell1 cell2 cell3 cell4 cell5 #> gene1     6     7     5     5     6 #> gene2     5     3     6     3     5 #> gene3     4     5     9     7     2 #> replace = TRUE),     coding = sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), size = length(gene_ids), replace = TRUE) ) head(rdata) #>       pathway coding #> gene1      P1  FALSE #> gene2      P1   TRUE #> gene3      P2   TRUE #> gene4      P1  FALSE #> gene5      P1   TRUE #> gene6      P1  FALSE  ## colData cdata <- data.frame(     row.names = cell_ids,      cell_type = sample(c("ct1", "ct2"), size = length(cell_ids), replace = TRUE) ) head(cdata) #>       cell_type #> cell1       ct2 #> cell2       ct2 #> cell3       ct2 #> cell4       ct1 #> cell5       ct2 #> cell6       ct1  ## Graph (with node attribute `degree`) g <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(     cor(t(mat)), mode = "undirected", weighted = TRUE ) g <- set_vertex_attr(g, "degree", value = strength(g)) g #> IGRAPH 2c53993 UNW- 200 20096 --  #> + attr: name (v/c), degree (v/n), weight (e/n) #> + edges from 2c53993 (vertex names): #>  [1] gene1--gene1  gene1--gene2  gene1--gene3  gene1--gene4  gene1--gene5  #>  [6] gene1--gene6  gene1--gene7  gene1--gene8  gene1--gene9  gene1--gene10 #> [11] gene1--gene11 gene1--gene12 gene1--gene13 gene1--gene14 gene1--gene15 #> [16] gene1--gene16 gene1--gene17 gene1--gene18 gene1--gene19 gene1--gene20 #> [21] gene1--gene21 gene1--gene22 gene1--gene23 gene1--gene24 gene1--gene25 #> [26] gene1--gene26 gene1--gene27 gene1--gene28 gene1--gene29 gene1--gene30 #> [31] gene1--gene31 gene1--gene32 gene1--gene33 gene1--gene34 gene1--gene35 #> [36] gene1--gene36 gene1--gene37 gene1--gene38 gene1--gene39 gene1--gene40 #> + ... omitted several edges # Create a `GraphExperiment` object ge <- GraphExperiment(     assays = list(counts = mat),     rowData = rdata,     colData = cdata,     graphs = list(cor = g) ) ge #> class: GraphExperiment  #> dim: 200 100  #> metadata(0): #> assays(1): counts #> rownames(200): gene1 gene2 ... gene199 gene200 #> rowData names(3): pathway coding cor__degree #> colnames(100): cell1 cell2 ... cell99 cell100 #> colData names(1): cell_type #> reducedDimNames(0): #> mainExpName: NULL #> altExpNames(0): #> graphs(1): cor # Remove 'gene1' to 'gene10' from the graph and try to recreate object g2 <- delete_vertices(g, paste0("gene", 1:10)) GraphExperiment(     assays = list(counts = mat),     rowData = rdata,     colData = cdata,     graphs = list(cor = g2) ) #> Error in `validObject()`: #> ! invalid class "GraphExperiment" object:  #> title: GraphExperiment S4 class — GraphExperiment-class
text: Like SingleCellExperiment, GraphExperiment S4 class stores quantitative data associated metadata (.e., rowData colData) along embeddings dimensionality reduction techniques. However, provides users additional container igraph objects containing graphs describing features interact . Graphs stored graphs slot, can hold one multiple igraph objects sort network representation features rownames. Example graphs can coexpression networks, regulatory networks, co-abundance networks. Importantly, node names graph must match rownames assays, subsetting methods simultaneously subset assays, rowData, graphs. Besides constructor function (GraphExperiment()), GraphExperiment object can also created coercing SummarizedExperiment SingleCellExperiment object.
